title: Degraded burst throttling threshold regression and customer impact mitigation
creator: Priya Nair
description: Short summary: Production regression in reserved-pool burst scoring led to aggressive headroom underestimation and premature throttling for several Dedicated tenants. Impact: multiple customers observed elevated 429/503s during burst windows and filed escalations (notable: StreamlineAI). Root cause: a change in the autoscaler candidate scoring (commit 3f9c2b) that introduced integer truncation when computing reserve_headroom for heterogenous GPU shapes. This produced negative headroom signals for low-latency classes and triggered early throttles and conservative placement decisions. Timeline: 2026-03-09 02:14 UTC first anomaly in metrics; 2026-03-09 04:30 customer escalations; 2026-03-10 hotfix rolled to prod; 2026-03-11 canary patch validated; 2026-03-12 full rollout complete. Current state: hotfix applied, incident mitigations in runbook, monitoring alerts tuned. Next steps: postmortem, stronger CI tests, invariant checks, and capacity planning audit.
actions_taken: 2026-03-10 hotfix deployed: restore floating-point calculation and add clamping to headroom computation
Temporary manual override: extended burst_limit by 25% for affected pools (marshalling reservation credits)
Canary rollout: patched clusters in us-west1 and eu-west1 first, observed noise reduction in token latency and 429 rate
Customer communication: sent incident blurb and mitigation notes to StreamlineAI and two other tenants
Alert tuning: added new SLO-based alert to detect rapid headroom drop and matched request throttling
rollback_plan: If regression reappears, revert commit 3f9c2b via emergency revert PR and engage allocator on-call to apply manual overrides to burst_limit and placement policy.
long_term_plan: Add unit and integration tests for headroom arithmetic across all GPU types
Introduce synthetic burst load tests in staging with multi-tenant variance
Implement invariant checker that prevents negative headroom signals from reaching allocator
Add a CanaryGate in CI that runs on autoscaler scoring changes against historical trace data
Document burst accounting and publish a dedicated DR runbook for reserved-pool shortfalls
notes: Engineering lead: Luca Moretti. Incident commander rotation: Priya Nair. Customer success-led comms coordinated by Maya Chen. Related customer ticket IDs provided in customer portal. Avoided full pool reboots to prevent longer disruptions.
